description: Drive the real Claude Code CLI against the local model double on a --unified-skills install, and check that every one of PAN's skills is listed to the model, so the model can invoke them.
why: 3.41.3 reverts market-ideas M49 (MI-132). With `disable-model-invocation: true` on PAN's Claude commands, Claude Code kept them from the model entirely: it could not start a PAN command for a plain request or chain one command into the next, so the user had to type every one. PAN's commands must be listed to the model, and this scenario is the observation that they are. The double answers from a script, so nothing is spent.

steps.why: One turn, so the host sends its full system prompt and tool list.
Every PAN command with a distinctive description reaches the model, so it can run one for a plain request or chain to the next step.
The user types the command, as PAN's docs tell them to.

args: Display the complete PAN command reference.
steps.why: The command still runs when the user types it: its body reaches the model.

write.content:
---
name: pan-help
description: Show available PAN commands and usage guide
disable-model-invocation: true
---

<objective>
Display the complete PAN command reference.
</objective>

controls.why: The same help entry marked disable-model-invocation must drop out of the listing, and the listing step alone must turn the scenario red.
